1.explanation:
To understand and reproduce this bug you need to see:  
1) How the user-timing audit currently pulls and filters (or doesn’t filter) marks from the trace (audits/user-timing-test.js).  
2) How those raw marks are then formatted for display in the report (formatter/user-timings-test.js and report/report-test.js).  
3) How the trace event stream is parsed and turned into timing marks (lib/traces/tracing-processor-test.js).  
4) How the audit results are aggregated and surfaced through the runner/aggregator pipeline (aggregator/aggregate-test.js and runner-test.js).  

Together these files cover the trace processing, audit logic, result aggregation, and final report formatting steps that lead to the unfiltered third-party User Timing marks appearing in the UI.
1.bug_scenario:
The screenshot shows Lighthouse’s “Performance: User Timing marks and measures” report flooded with third-party metrics (e.g. “ad_slots_defined”, “ad_requested_from_server”, “ad_rendering_complete” and dozens of “goog_…” start/end marks) injected by Google Ads. Instead of only developer-defined User Timing marks, the audit is including all marks in the trace, making the list enormous and hiding the meaningful timings.

Key on-screen elements:
- The large count (“2163”) of reported marks/measures
- Marks prefixed with “ad_” (ad_slots_defined, ad_first_ad_rendered, ad_rendering_complete x N)
- Marks prefixed with “goog_” (goog_123_3_1_start, goog_123_3_1_end, etc.)
- The Lighthouse sidebar and performance section indicating this is the User Timing audit
